author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating: this is a significant refactor (6 public functions across emit/parse/catalog/profile, plus tests) with three viable options that have meaningfully different cost/value trade-offs. Doing the work autonomously would commit ~500+ lines of API churn on a maintainer-judgment call about whether the architectural cleanliness is worth that effort relative to the (low) probability of serde_json 2.0.

Options considered:

(1) Return String / &str / Vec<u8> on emit; accept &str / &[u8] on parse. Cleanest API surface, no foreign type leakage. Costs: forces serialization on every emit even for callers who walk the JSON DOM in-memory; existing tests use serde_json::Value heavily for in-memory composition and would need substantial rework (serialize-then-parse to inspect emit output).

(2) Opaque newtype wrappers (OscalAssessmentResults, OscalCatalog, OscalProfile, OscalRisks) carrying serde_json::Value internally with methods like as_json_value(), to_string_pretty(), from_str(). Highest architectural completeness; preserves the in-memory Value workflow for callers who want it; pkix-lint absorbs serde_json major bumps internally for the common case. Costs: ~30 lines per type × 4 types ≈ 120 lines of new wrapper code, plus all 6 public functions' signatures change, plus all tests update to call the new constructors/accessors. Still leaks serde_json::Value through the escape-hatch as_json_value() method — partial decoupling, not full.

(3) Document the serde_json major-version pin commitment explicitly in the oscal/mod.rs module rustdoc and accept the pin. Cheapest option. The bead notes this is 'a real cost the maintainer should make deliberately, not by default.'

Recommendation: option (3). Rationale: (a) serde_json has been at 1.x stable for ~9 years with no signal of a 2.0; this is among the lowest-probability dependency-version risks in the workspace's tree. (b) The opaque-newtype shape (option 2) still leaks serde_json::Value through as_json_value(), so the decoupling is partial — full decoupling requires option (1) which has a higher test-churn cost than the bead acknowledges. (c) AGENTS.md pre-launch frame says 'design for the eventual complete shape' but the architecturally complete shape for OSCAL emit/parse is genuinely 'we produce/consume JSON' — wrapping that in opaque newtypes is one layer of indirection that doesn't fundamentally change the shape. (d) The competing options' costs are real (test rework for option 1, surface-area expansion for option 2); a documented pin commits to maintaining stable behavior under one constraint rather than introducing a wrapper API that's tested less than serde_json itself.

If the maintainer prefers option (2) (opaque newtypes), the migration is mechanically straightforward and I can execute it in a subsequent /do-beads pass — just leave a 'do option 2' comment on this bead. Same for option (1).
